gappers.catalyst: No company news dated 11/25-11/27; move is a bounce off the 11/25 52-week-area low after a 31% three-week de-rate, despite a Nov 5 Q3 beat-and-raise.
headlines: BlackSky Q3 2026: revenue $42.8M (+118% YoY) vs $39.55M est, GAAP EPS $0.10 vs -$0.22 est, net income $18.5M, cash $231M, FY guidance raised (Nov 5, 2026 8-K)
BlackSky wins seven-figure Assured contract with new major international ministry of defense (~Nov 10, 2026)
Shares tumbled in a risk-off session for tech and space names even after the company's results
gappers.catalyst_detail: There is no fresh company-specific catalyst today. BlackSky's last material news was a strong one: the Nov 5 Q3 2026 report showed revenue of $42.8M, up 118% YoY and ahead of the $39.55M consensus, GAAP EPS of $0.10 against a -$0.22 estimate, net income of $18.5M versus a $15.3M loss a year earlier, $231M of cash, and raised full-year revenue and adjusted-EBITDA guidance. A seven-figure Assured subscription contract with a new international ministry of defense followed around Nov 10. Despite both, the stock fell from a 60-day high of $24.92 to a $14.62 low on 11/25 in a broad risk-off de-rating of space and speculative-growth names. Today's +7.8% is the second up-day off that low. The most recent 424B5 shelf takedown is dated 2026-05-22, so no equity offering explains the November decline.
gappers.why: Mechanically this is short-covering and dip-buying off a capitulation low, not a response to news. The fundamental catalyst (beat and raise) is three weeks stale and was already sold through; what changed is that selling pressure exhausted at $14.62 and a holiday-thinned tape lets small buy flow move price a long way. Sector read-through is the whole driver: the decline was sector-wide across space names, so the bounce is too.
gappers.impact: Reads as a low-conviction technical bounce, not a sustainable move. Volume is the tell: 322,932 shares by 10:13 ET against a 20-day average of 1,190,397, about 27% of normal, and this is a half session closing at 13:00 ET. A genuine reversal off a multi-week low needs above-average volume, not a quarter of it. Price is still 31% below the 60-day high and well under both SMA20 ($19.81) and SMA50 ($20.08), so the trend is intact to the downside and this is counter-trend. ATR14 is $1.81, 10.5% of price, so a 7.8% day is less than one ATR and inside normal noise for this name. Peer read-through: AMPX, the other qualifier, bottomed the same day (11/25) and is bouncing the same amount, confirming this is a market-wide speculative-growth bounce rather than anything BlackSky-specific.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: No new catalyst, price below both SMA20 and SMA50, and the move is sub-1-ATR on 27% of average volume. The durable part of the thesis (beat, raise, defense contracts) was already rejected by the tape for three weeks, so there is no structural trigger to carry past the session.
gappers.opportunity_cost: The account is 100% cash with 0 positions and 0 open orders, so this displaces no existing holding. The binding constraints are the 3-new-trades-per-week budget and the Confluence rule, which this setup fails on trend alignment: price is below SMA20 and SMA50 on a counter-trend bounce. R:R is marginal at best. A compliant 10% trailing stop from $17.21 sits at $15.49, risking $1.72/share (0.95 ATR), so the 2:1 minimum needs $20.65 - which lands directly in the SMA20/SMA50 resistance band at $19.81/$20.08. The reward leg has to punch through three weeks of overhead supply to pay, so the 2:1 does not clear cleanly at a sane stop. ATR sizing would allow 552 shares (~$9,500, 9.5% of equity), inside the 20% cap, but spending one of three weekly trades on a sub-1-ATR counter-trend bounce in a half session at 27% of normal volume is the expensive part. The higher-ranked alternative from today's own list is nothing - this IS rank 1 of 2, and rank 2 (AMPX) is a worse version of the same trade. Research only; no order.

gappers.catalyst: No company news today; bounce off the 11/25 one-year low after a post-Q3 de-rate that cut the stock 46% from its 60-day high.
headlines: Amprius Q3 2026: sales $39.15M, net loss narrowed, but adjusted EBITDA swung to -$1.0M from +$0.2M a year earlier (reported Nov 10, 2026)
Shares fell 7.87% Wednesday 11/25 to ~$5.27 intraday in a broad risk-off session; no company release accompanied the drop
Background: Manatee Research short report alleging illusory orders and a 'Potemkin village' manufacturing network - dated May 2026, not November
gappers.catalyst_detail: No fresh catalyst today; a third-party finance tracker explicitly logged 'no new macro, sector, or company-specific catalysts detected.' The relevant history is the Nov 10 Q3 2026 print: sales of $39.15M with the net loss narrowed, but adjusted EBITDA swung negative to -$1.0M from +$0.2M a year earlier, which is the line most coverage blames for the de-rate. The stock then fell in steps - down 10.5% on 11/20, a new one-year low on 11/24, and down 7.87% to ~$5.27 intraday on 11/25 - with no company release attached to any of them. Today's +6.7% is a bounce off that low. Note on provenance: the Manatee Research short report alleging at least $29M of illusory LEV orders, a fraudulent or subscale partner network, and bill-and-hold accounting is dated May 2026. It is background on why the name carries a high short base (~21% of float per one secondary source), not a November event, and it should not be cited as today's catalyst.
gappers.why: Same mechanism as BKSY and no more than that: selling exhausted at a one-year low and a heavily shorted, high-beta small cap snaps back on thin holiday flow. With a large short base, even modest buy pressure forces covering, which exaggerates the percentage move relative to the dollar flow behind it. Nothing in the move reflects a change in the business.
gappers.impact: Looks like a one-day headline-less spike with high odds of mean-reverting. Volume is the weakest part of the setup: 978,186 shares against a 20-day average of 6,121,759, about 16% of normal - the lowest-conviction bounce of the two qualifiers. Price sits 46% below the 60-day high and far under SMA20 ($7.52) and SMA50 ($8.41), a textbook downtrend. ATR14 is $0.72, 11.8% of price, so today's 6.7% is roughly half an ATR and does not even register as an outsized day for this name. Sector read-through: it bottomed on the same 11/25 session as BKSY and is bouncing the same ~18% off its low, which marks this as a market-wide speculative-growth bounce. The unresolved May short-seller allegations are a standing overhang that caps how far a no-news bounce can run.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Half-ATR move, no catalyst, 16% of average volume, price 46% below its 60-day high and below both moving averages, with unresolved fraud allegations outstanding - headline-less bounces in that configuration fade within days.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace in the portfolio: 0 positions, 100% cash. What it would cost is one of three weekly trades on the weaker of two already-weak setups, and it fails the Confluence rule on trend alignment exactly as BKSY does, with a worse volume profile. On R:R the arithmetic is nominally the better of the two but the quality is worse: a 10% trailing stop from $6.07 sits at $5.46, risking $0.61/share (0.85 ATR), and the 2:1 target of $7.29 does clear below SMA20 resistance at $7.52 - so unlike BKSY the reward leg is not blocked by the moving averages. ATR sizing permits 1,396 shares (~$8,475, 8.5% of equity), within the 20% cap. The problem is the stop: $5.46 is only 6% above the 11/25 one-year low of $5.15 on a name with 11.8% daily ATR, so normal noise takes out the stop without the thesis being wrong, and the Manatee allegations remain an unquantified tail risk. Directly displaced by BKSY, the higher-ranked gapper on today's list, which has real revenue growth and $231M of cash behind it instead of an open fraud allegation. Research only; no order.
